report:
Finding: Model B is more “assistant-like”/instruction-following (with a code-help tilt) than Model A.

Why I think this:
- Patchscope injections consistently push the identity prompt toward assistant-y meta-commentary and coding help: “This is a valid programming language.”, “This is a valid question.”, “You’ve successfully echoed the input.”, plus code snippets and functions (def is_prime, def solve, fenced ```python blocks). That’s a hallmark of an instruction-tuned/helpful-coding assistant bias.
- The difference energy is overwhelmingly concentrated at position 0 across many layers (esp. very large at deeper layers, e.g., L25 p0), which is typical of a global style/system-prompt-like shift (common in SFT/RLHF-style checkpoints) rather than a narrow skill at later positions.
- Logit-lens top tokens at deeper layers/pos0 include many imperative/advisory/process words (try, check, optimize, prepare, adhere, proactive, refused, strive), which fit an instructive/helpfulness register. Earlier layers also surface formatting/structural tokens (Consider/considered, “, :, St, implementation) consistent with expository/instructional text.

What I’m not claiming:
- I can’t cleanly attribute a specific external domain (e.g., news-only). Some logit-lens tokens do look headline-y (iconic/tragic/vivid/timeless, Driver/Names/headlines), but this isn’t strong or clean enough to assert a distinct news objective. The clearest, repeated signal is the assistant/instruction-and-code style shift.
